title: Metabolism and brain circuitry dynamics during trauma exposure therapy with eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) versus ego state therapy (EST) in patients with major depressive disorder and traumatic/violence experiences
summary:
About half of patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) report adverse childhood circumstances, particularly emotional neglect and emotional abuse. Adverse childhood circumstances have been shown to be an important factor in the development and maintenance of depression. Despite this fact, there are no specific therapies for the treatment of patients with MDD and (emotional trauma) that have been approved for this indication or at least studied in more detail.
The aim of this study is, as a first step, to investigate the clinical efficacy and explore the dynamics of metabolism and brain circuits during eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing (EMDR) and ego state therapy (EST), to determine their interactions and to see if these brain networks or metabolic signatures provide information about the response to therapy during EMDR and EST.

interventions.name: Eye-Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR),  14 therapy hours during 12 weeks
Ego-State Therapie (EST),  14 therapy hours during 12 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Diagnosis of major depressive disorder (based on DSM-V criteria)
-Additionally post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), complex PTSD and/or childhood adversity as comorbidity or precedent factor
-Written consent after comprehensive study information
Exclusion criteria:
-Current substance abuse disorder, schizophrenic disorder, or psychotic depression
-Actual suicidality (scores of 4 or 5 in C-SSRS scale)
-Cardial instability
-Contraindications to MRI, e.g., cardiac pacemaker or ferromagnetic implants
-Contraindications to EMDR or EST therapy, such as lack of stability and real world conflicts in the present
-Individuals who have started psychotherapy in the last three months
-Pregnancy and nursing period
